Outlet: GOV.UK (DCMS; The Rt Hon Wes Streeting MP, The Rt Hon Andy Burnham MP, The Rt Hon Lisa Nandy MP), published 8 November 2026

The King to lead nation in silence on Remembrance Sunday

His Majesty The King will lead the UK in the annual two-minute silence to remember those who have fallen and suffered in conflict at the National Service of Remembrance at the Cenotaph. The King will be joined by members of The Royal Family, the Prime Minister, senior politicians and faith representatives to mark the Armistice of the First World War and all other conflicts involving British and Commonwealth forces.

Approximately 10,000 veterans will take part in the Royal British Legion's March Past, with over 300 different Armed Forces and civilian organisations represented. Members of The Royal Family and senior politicians will lay wreaths at the National Service of Remembrance at the Cenotaph in London. Approximately 10,000 members of the public are expected to line Whitehall.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated: "Remembrance Sunday gives us an opportunity to mark sacrifice and offer gratitude" and reflects on the "selflessness and courage" required in military service. [fetch tool paraphrase around quoted fragments]

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy remarked: "It is our duty to ensure that the immense courage of those who have served is never forgotten."

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting noted: "We have a moral duty to stand by our veterans and military families who sacrifice so much."

The national event will be broadcast live on the BBC, ITV and Sky News.
